subject: Usage-slab pricing & true-up cadence for Orion Health integration
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@orionhealth.ai>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Usage-slab pricing proposal and monthly true-up cadence

Hi Samira —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Attached is our updated proposal (orion-proposal-v3.pdf) and a live pricing model (pricing-model-Orion.xlsx) that shows how the usage slabs map to monthly invoices.

High-level summary:
- Commitment: 12-month committed usage starting Jan 1, 2027.
- Billing: monthly invoicing with a monthly true-up against committed tokens.
- Pricing: slab ("usage-slab") tiers with step-down per-token rates as you hit higher usage buckets.

Key asks from us:
1) Confirm the committed monthly baseline (you mentioned ~1.2B tokens/month as a starting point).
2) Agree to a monthly true-up (overage billed at slab rates; underuse credits applied to next month).
3) Confirm whether you prefer a single blended effective rate for forecasting or explicit marginal slab rates on invoices.

Why slabs: slabs let us give aggressive per-token rates at scale while keeping monthly billing predictable. We can also provide an optional blended reporting view in the invoice if that helps your FP&A team.

I realize we haven't pinned down whether you want marginal (each extra token charged at the rate for the slab it falls into) or blended (a single average $/token for the whole month based on total usage). Both are workable; below is what we typically see:
- Marginal: cleaner from a supplier perspective (transparent step-downs) but can be harder to forecast for finance.
- Blended: easier for forecasting and internal chargeback — you get one number per month but we build reconciliation logic during true-up.

If it helps, I can send a short worked example with numbers (both marginal and blended) showing how a sample month at 3.7B tokens would invoice. Would you like that?

Attachments: orion-proposal-v3.pdf (proposal), pricing-model-Orion.xlsx (live model)

Thanks,

Team —

FYI — Samira asked for a side-by-side worked example of marginal vs blended and confirmed they prefer monthly true-up. Procurement also asked for a redline of the term-sheet.

Proposed approach (my recommendation):
- Keep slab/marginal as our default pricing (it preserves upside at scale).
- Offer an invoice-level blended view as an export (reporting-only) to help their FP&A. No change to how charges are computed — blended is for reporting/forecasting only.
- Accept monthly true-up (we price conservatively to protect unit economics; add a 30% overage cap if they spike >3x month-over-month to avoid abuse).

Concessions we can make:
1) If they sign 12-month commit at >=15B tokens/month peak, drop the top slab by $0.0025/token for the final tier.
2) One-time onboarding credit equal to 2 weeks of committed baseline usage applied in month 1.

Legal: please attach a redline that keeps standard data residency and audit clauses but adds explicit monthly true-up language and escrow for charge disputes.

Attaching: redlines-term-sheet.docx (draft for legal)

Rachel

Subject: Re: Usage-slab pricing proposal and monthly true-up cadence

Hi Samira —

Thanks — attached are the two worked examples and an updated term-sheet redline (attachments). Below is a short, plain-English summary plus the numeric examples you asked for.

Summary of commercial model we propose:
- Commitment: 12 months, baseline 1.2B tokens/month.
- Slab structure (per-token):
  * 0 - 5B tokens/month: $0.0090 / token
  * 5B - 20B tokens/month: $0.0065 / token
  * >20B tokens/month: $0.0045 / token
- Billing mechanics:
  * Marginal (default): each token charged at the slab rate where it falls (common supplier model).
  * Blended (reporting view only): invoice will include an additional line showing an effective $/token for the month computed as (total billed amount) / (total tokens). This does not change charge calculation, only reporting.
- True-up cadence: monthly (we will invoice actual usage; if actual < committed baseline, credit applied forward; if actual > committed baseline, overage billed at slab/marginal rates).
- Protections: a monthly spike protection clause — any month with >3x the prior month usage will be capped at 3x for invoice purposes; we can discuss an exception path for carefully scoped piloting.
- Concessions included for Orion: 1) onboarding credit = two weeks of baseline usage applied month 1; 2) if 12-month commit averaged >=15B tokens/month we will reduce top-slab rate to $0.0020 / token for months after threshold achieved.

Worked example (single representative month with 3.7B tokens):
A) Marginal computation
  - First 3.7B tokens fall in 0 - 5B slab, charged at $0.0090 -> Invoice = 3,700,000,000 * $0.0090 = $33,300,000
  - Effective blended $/token = $33,300,000 / 3,700,000,000 = $0.0090 (since only first slab used)

B) Blended scenario example (for a month with 18.6B tokens total)
  - Marginal steps:
    * 0-5B @ $0.0090 -> 5,000,000,000 * $0.0090 = $45,000,000
    * 5-18.6B (13.6B) @ $0.0065 -> 13,600,000,000 * $0.0065 = $88,400,000
    * Total invoice = $133,400,000
    * Blended effective rate = $133,400,000 / 18,600,000,000 = $0.00717/token (we will show this as a reporting line on the invoice)

Operational notes:
- We'll provide a CSV export with row-level token buckets per region per day so you can validate charges quickly during the true-up window.
- Dispute window: 30 days from invoice date; we will hold disputed amounts in escrow while both teams reconcile.
- DocuSign link (included below) will be updated with these terms once you confirm the commit baseline.

Attachments included: orion-proposal-v3.pdf, pricing-model-Orion.xlsx, redlines-term-sheet.docx
